contentHtml:
GERMANY—Hong Kong Science and Technology Parks Corporation (HKSTP) led its first delegation of 22 technology companies and university partners to MEDICA 2026 in Düsseldorf from November 16 to 19, seeking European partnerships and international markets for Hong Kong and Chinese Mainland medical technologies.

Working with the Hong Kong Trade Development Council (HKTDC) and the Hong Kong MedTech Association, HKSTP facilitated business engagements, technology showcases, and agreements with European healthcare industry players.

Partnerships target European market access

A key development was the signing of memoranda of understanding (MoUs) with Germany’s Medical Valley EMN and Kalms Consulting.

The agreement with Medical Valley will support market access, business matching, clinical research, innovation and stakeholder engagement.

Meanwhile, the partnership with Kalms Consulting will help Hong Kong companies navigate European regulatory requirements, commercialisation and business development.

HKSTP Chief Executive Officer Terry Wong said international partnerships were essential to translating research breakthroughs into healthcare solutions.

He noted that the agreements would establish cross-border channels for regulatory support and market access, while helping technology companies connect their research with international commercial opportunities.

The delegation also facilitated agreements between individual companies.

Orange Biotech, which develops CRISPR-based diagnostic platforms, signed an MoU with Hungarian medical device company CorLab to explore distribution of its point-of-care testing products in Hungary and other European Union markets.

The agreement also covers regulatory requirements, commercialisation and potential future manufacturing and assembly in Hungary.

In another agreement, Pushkang Biotechnology partnered with Egypt-based Keen Diagnostic Partners (KDP) to introduce and commercialise its MS200 Automated Chemistry Analyzer and associated reagent panels in Egypt.

The partnership combines Pushkang’s microfluidic technology with KDP’s local healthcare network to support product distribution, training and market development.

Companies showcase diagnostic innovations

HKSTP companies also presented new technologies to international buyers and healthcare professionals.

AusMed Global marked the European soft launch of KetoMetrics®, a CE-marked portable breath ketone monitoring device designed to provide real-time metabolic measurements in clinical and home settings.

The company positions the technology for applications in weight management, sports performance, healthy ageing and ketogenic interventions.

Meanwhile, Dymind introduced its upgraded, CE-marked DH-8000 haematology analysis workstation for large laboratories.

The system supports complete blood count (CBC), C-reactive protein (CRP), serum amyloid A (SAA) and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) testing, with expandable modules for sample processing and slide preparation.

Strengthening Asia-Europe cooperation

Beyond the exhibition, HKSTP organised an executive roundtable with international law firm Clifford Chance to discuss MedTech collaboration.

The delegation also visited Siemens Healthineers, Würth Group, TUM Venture Labs and SGS Germany to explore opportunities in regulation, investment, research and commercialisation.

HKSTP arranged business meetings with organisations including Deloitte, DQS, High-Tech Gründerfonds, Intertek, SGS and Tekno Surgical.

Wong also addressed MEDICA’s Market Entry Stage, highlighting Hong Kong’s research capabilities, clinical resources and role as a gateway to Asian markets.

HKSTP supports more than 400 life and health technology companies through funding, incubation, research infrastructure and industry connections, helping them progress from research and development to commercialisation and international expansion.
